title: Go Signal
teaches: The Go Signal as we trade it, on hourly bars: a leader in an uptrend pulls back to support, the first hourly candle trades under the prior day's close, and buyers push it back above that close by the end of the second hourly candle. The stop sits a few cents under the session low at the time of entry, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, and a turn after the second candle is a pivot, not a Go Signal.

questions.q: On a Go Signal, red to green is measured against which price?
choices: The prior day's close
The hourly candle's own open
The flag low
The session VWAP
questions.why: The prior day's close. Red to green is measured against the prior day's close, not the candle's own open and not a flag low.
questions.lesson_line: The line is yesterday's close. Nothing else.

wrong.The hourly candle's own open: A candle that merely closes above its own open is green, not a Go Signal. The line is the prior close.
wrong.The flag low: The card says it is not measured against a flag low.
wrong.The session VWAP: VWAP is not the line here. The Go Signal reads the prior day's close.

questions.q: A Go Signal needs the first hourly candle to trade below the prior day's close.
questions.why: True. Early in the session the stock trades under the prior day's close, then buyers push it back above.
questions.lesson_line: Under the prior close first, then back over it.

questions.q: By the end of which hourly candle must the stock be back above the prior close?
choices: The second
The first only
The fourth
The last of the day
questions.why: The second. The reclaim comes by the end of the second hourly candle. A turn after that is a pivot, not a Go Signal.
questions.lesson_line: First or second candle. After that it is a pivot.

wrong.The first only: The first or the second candle counts. A turn in the second is still a Go Signal.
wrong.The fourth: By the fourth candle it is a pivot, not a Go Signal.
wrong.The last of the day: A turn that late is a pivot. The Go Signal lives in the first two candles.

questions.q: A gap up that never trades under the prior close is a Go Signal.
questions.why: False. A gap up that never trades under the prior close is not a Go Signal. The dip under the prior close comes first.
questions.lesson_line: No dip under the prior close, no Go Signal.

questions.q: What do we call a turn that comes after the second hourly candle?
choices: A pivot, not a Go Signal
A Go Signal, but a late one
An Oops at the prior low
A Remount of the line
questions.answer: A pivot, not a Go Signal
questions.why: A pivot, not a Go Signal. A turn later in the day, however clean, is a 30-minute pivot bought over the pivot candle's high.
questions.lesson_line: After the second candle, it is a pivot.

wrong.A Go Signal, but a late one: There is no late version. After the second candle it is a pivot.
wrong.An Oops at the prior low: An Oops is a daily-bar pattern at the prior day's low.
wrong.A Remount of the line: A Remount retakes a line lost over a long stay. This is one session.

questions.q: The Go Signal turn is read on hourly bars, not on the daily chart.
questions.why: True. The daily footprint cannot show the turn, so grading from the daily chart is a listed mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Hourly bars show the turn. The daily chart hides it.

questions.q: A Go Signal needs the stock above its 200-day SMA.
questions.why: True. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. The card also wants the price above the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day, or no Go Signal.

questions.lesson_line: Green, yes. Orange, A plus. Red, none.

wrong.Only the A plus ones: A plus only is Orange. On Red there are none.
wrong.Half size on each: Smaller size is the Yellow reading. Red is none.
wrong.As many as show up: The market reading limits the book. Red means mostly cash.

questions.q: What makes a Go Signal more than a bare red to green?

The hour the turn comes in
The size of the candle
The ticker's share price

wrong.The ticker's share price: Price only has to pass the liquidity rule.

questions.why: True. The card wants the price above the 50-day, and lists a Go Signal in a downtrend, under the 50-day or 200-day, as a mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 50-day and the 200-day.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A trade still under 1R after ___ trading days is sold.
questions.why: 10. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days under 1R: out.

questions.q: A clean turn at 14:00 is still a Go Signal if the candle is strong.
questions.why: False. A turn after the second hourly candle is a pivot, not a Go Signal, however clean the candle.
questions.lesson_line: The clock decides. After the second candle it is a pivot.

questions.q: How does an Oops differ from a Go Signal?
choices: The Oops is a daily bar at the prior low
The Oops uses hourly bars
The Oops uses the prior close
They are the same
questions.answer: The Oops is a daily bar at the prior low
questions.why: The Oops is a daily bar at the prior low. An Oops gaps below the prior day's low and closes back above it; the Go Signal's line is the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Oops: daily, prior low. Go Signal: hourly, prior close.

wrong.The Oops uses hourly bars: The Oops is read on the daily bar. The Go Signal is read on the first two hourly candles.
wrong.The Oops uses the prior close: The Oops line is the prior day's low. The Go Signal line is the prior day's close.

questions.q: A Go Signal wants a 20-day EMA that is higher than it was 5 sessions ago.
questions.why: True. The card wants a rising 20-day EMA. The test is that it is higher than it was 5 sessions ago.
questions.lesson_line: The 20-day EMA should be rising.

questions.q: Entry 37.18. The session low is 36.15 and the stop sits 3 cents under it. How far below the entry, in percent?
questions.why: 2.85%. The stop is a few cents under the session low. It sits inside the 3% the stop usually sits within, so it fits.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop in percent before you size it.

questions.q: Prior close 168.84. The reclaim candle closes at 169.79. How far over the prior close, in percent?
questions.why: 0.6%. That is nowhere near 4% over the prior close, the buy point, so the chase rule does not block it.
questions.lesson_line: Check the distance from the prior close before you buy.

questions.q: Bought at 24.48 with the stop at 24.01. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 25.89. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. The first third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open.

questions.q: Buy?
choices: No, a report inside 3 sessions
Yes, the setup is too good to skip
Yes, but only at half size
Yes, with a tight stop
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before an earnings report. A clean setup does not change the calendar.
questions.lesson_line: Report inside 3 sessions: no new buy.

wrong.Yes, the setup is too good to skip: The setup passes. The calendar does not.
wrong.Yes, but only at half size: Half size is still a new buy inside the window.
wrong.Yes, with a tight stop: A tight stop does not lift the earnings rule.

questions.story: A perfect first-hour reclaim at the 20-day line. The stock reports earnings in two sessions.

questions.q: Is this a Go Signal?
choices: No; it never went red first
Yes, it is green all morning
Yes, if the 20-day is rising
Yes, it held green after 11:00
questions.answer: No; it never went red first
questions.why: No. A gap up that never trades under the prior close is not a Go Signal. The dip under it comes first.
questions.lesson_line: No red, no red to green.

wrong.Yes, it is green all morning: Green is not red to green. There was no red first.
wrong.Yes, if the 20-day is rising: A rising 20-day is context. Without a dip under the prior close there is no signal.
wrong.Yes, it held green after 11:00: Time does not create the dip. A late turn is a pivot anyway.

questions.story: The stock opens 0.8% above the prior close and never trades under it. It grinds green all morning.

questions.q: U&R or Go Signal?
choices: A Go Signal on the hourly bars
A U&R; it undercut and reclaimed
A Remount of the prior close
An Oops at the prior low
questions.answer: A Go Signal on the hourly bars
questions.why: A Go Signal. Its undercut and reclaim happen inside the first two hours of one session and are measured against the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: One session, prior close, hourly: a Go Signal.

wrong.A U&R; it undercut and reclaimed: A U&R takes back a level over up to 3 sessions on the daily chart. This is one session, hourly.
wrong.A Remount of the prior close: A Remount follows a line lost for days. The prior close is one day old.
wrong.An Oops at the prior low: An Oops is a daily bar at the prior low. This line is the prior close.

questions.story: In one session the first hourly candle dips under the prior close. The second hourly candle closes back above it.

questions.q: Sell at the close, or hold?
choices: Hold; it is a warning, not an exit
Sell at the close; the turn failed
Move the stop up to 90.55
Add on the dip
questions.answer: Hold; it is a warning, not an exit
questions.why: Hold. A day that closes back under the prior close is a warning, not an exit. NVDA closed at 90.41 and was stopped the next day at 89.39.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the prior close is a warning. The stop is the exit.

wrong.Sell at the close; the turn failed: Selling at that close did not improve the average. The stop is the exit.
wrong.Move the stop up to 90.55: Never raise the stop to the reclaimed level.
wrong.Add on the dip: Full size at one price with one stop. No adding.

questions.story: You bought a first-candle reclaim at 90.98 with the stop at 89.39. At 15:50 the stock is 90.41, under the prior close 90.55, above your stop.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Get out; that low is past 2R
Set the stop at 118.83 and hold
Keep the 123.39 stop and wait
Buy more at the lower price
questions.answer: Get out; that low is past 2R
questions.why: Get out. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low, but if that takes the loss past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: First 30 minutes decide. Past 2R, out.

wrong.Set the stop at 118.83 and hold: The first 30-minute low is the new stop, but only up to a ceiling. Past 2R, you are out.
wrong.Keep the 123.39 stop and wait: The stock is already through it. The gap rule hands the stop to the first 30 minutes.
wrong.Buy more at the lower price: No adding, and never into a gap against the stop.

questions.story: You bought at 126.81 with the stop at 123.39, so 1R is 3.42. The next morning gaps down to 121.00. The first 30-minute low is 118.83.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Take a third off at the open
Wait for 25.89 on the way down
Hold it all and trail it up
Sell it all at the open now
questions.answer: Take a third off at the open
questions.why: Take the first third at the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Gap past a trim level: take it at the open.

wrong.Wait for 25.89 on the way down: You may never see it again. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
wrong.Hold it all and trail it up: The trail is for the last third, after the trims.
wrong.Sell it all at the open now: The plan is a third at 3R, a third at 5R, then the trail.

questions.story: You bought at 24.48 with the stop at 24.01. Your 3R level is 25.89. The next morning the stock opens at 26.40.

questions.q: What trails the last third of a fast Go Signal?
choices: A close under the 10-day line
A close under the 200-day line
A new 5-day closing low
The session low
questions.why: A close under the 10-day average. The 21-day suits a steady stock; sell on a close below it. Kullamagi trails the 10- or 20-day.
questions.lesson_line: Fast stock, 10-day. Steady stock, 21-day.

wrong.A close under the 200-day line: That is too slow for a fast stock. The 21-day suits a steadier one.
wrong.A new 5-day closing low: A short-term low is not our trail. We use the 10-day or the 21-day.
wrong.The session low: That is the first stop. After the trims it moves up and the trail takes over.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Sell; under 1R at 10 sessions
Hold; the stop has not been hit
Add to it while it is quiet
Move the stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, which frees the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten sessions, under 1R: out.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not been hit: The stop is not the only exit. A trade still under 1R after 10 sessions is sold.
wrong.Add to it while it is quiet: We do not add. The money is better used on a new setup.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven: Breakeven comes at 2R to 5R, not at 0.4R.

questions.story: Ten sessions after the buy, the stock sits at 0.4R. The stop has not been hit and no trim has come off.

questions.q: Skip the buy if the reclaim candle closes more than 4% above the prior close.
questions.why: True. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point, and here the buy point is the prior close. Chasing costs size, not risk.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the prior close and I am done.

questions.q: Account 100,000, risk 0.25%. Buy 336.42, stop 331.63. How many shares does the stop allow?
questions.why: 52 shares. The size comes from the stop: risk divided by the distance, rounded down. The 40% position cap is not close. That was META's stop, 1.42% from the buy.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. Not the other way round.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Size down or skip; never raise the stop
Raise the stop to the reclaimed level
Buy full size anyway
Use the 20-day EMA as the stop
questions.answer: Size down or skip; never raise the stop
questions.why: Size down or skip. If the stop is more than about 3% away, size down or skip; never raise it to the reclaimed level.
questions.lesson_line: Wide stop: fewer shares, or no trade.

wrong.Raise the stop to the reclaimed level: Never raise the stop to the reclaimed level. That is where the shake-out happens.
wrong.Buy full size anyway: The size comes from the stop. A wide stop means fewer shares or no trade.
wrong.Use the 20-day EMA as the stop: The stop is under the session low. An average is not the stop.

questions.story: A clean Go Signal sets up. The honest stop, a few cents under the session low, is 5.5% below the buy.

questions.q: The turn is valid. What do you do?
choices: Size down from the stop, or skip
Buy full size at the close
Tighten the stop to 3% to fit
Buy the open and skip the wait
questions.answer: Size down from the stop, or skip
questions.why: Size down from the stop, or skip. CRS was a valid turn whose first candle was too big to buy at its close.
questions.lesson_line: A giant first candle widens the stop. Size follows the stop.

wrong.Buy full size at the close: The first candle was too big to buy at its close at full size.
wrong.Tighten the stop to 3% to fit: Never tighten the stop to fit. It marks the real low.
wrong.Buy the open and skip the wait: The open is before the turn. Buying it is the blind open buy.

questions.story: After a 2.8% gap down the first candle runs from 315.73 to 329.02. The stop under its low is 4.96% from the entry.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Yes, a new trade, its own stop
No, it already failed on Monday
Yes, with a wider stop this time
Yes, at double size
questions.answer: Yes, a new trade, its own stop
questions.why: Yes, as a new trade with its own stop. A failed Go Signal that sets up again is a new trade, at most 3 tries a week and 6 a month.
questions.lesson_line: A new trigger is a new trade. Count the tries.

wrong.No, it already failed on Monday: A new trigger is a new trade. The limit is 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop this time: A wider stop to get back in is the mistake, not the fix.
wrong.Yes, at double size: Doubling to win it back makes a small loss bigger.

questions.story: A Go Signal in this stock failed on Monday. On Wednesday it sets up and turns again, a fresh trigger.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Pass; Orange allows only A plus
Take it at full size
Take it; Orange is Green with a tint
Take it and skip the stop
questions.answer: Pass; Orange allows only A plus
questions.why: Pass. Orange allows only A+ setups. Green is full risk, Yellow is smaller and fewer, and Red is mostly cash.
questions.lesson_line: Orange means A plus only. A B waits.

wrong.Take it at full size: Full risk is the Green reading. Orange allows only A+ setups.
wrong.Take it; Orange is Green with a tint: Orange is two steps down from Green. It allows only A+ setups.

questions.story: The market reading is Orange. A Go Signal sets up cleanly, but you grade it a B.

questions.q: Heavy volume on the reclaim is a hard rule for the Go Signal.
questions.why: False. Volume is not a rule. More volume on the reclaim than on the flag's first hours is a plus for grading.
questions.lesson_line: Volume grades the signal. It does not gate it.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Pass; no longs under the 200-day
Take it; the 20-day is rising
Take it at half size
Take it if the market is Green
questions.why: Pass. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. A Go Signal is not one.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day is a hard line. Under it, no Go Signal.

wrong.Take it; the 20-day is rising: A rising 20-day is one gate. The 200-day is another, and it is a hard rule.
wrong.Take it at half size: Half size does not lift a hard rule.
wrong.Take it if the market is Green: A Green market does not lift the 200-day rule.

questions.story: A textbook first-hour reclaim at a rising 20-day EMA. The stock is under its 200-day SMA.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Pass; it is in a downtrend
Take it; the turn is clean
Take it; downtrends bounce
Take it on the second candle only
questions.answer: Pass; it is in a downtrend
questions.why: Pass. Taking a Go Signal in a downtrend, under the 50-day or 200-day, is a listed mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Leaders in uptrends only.

wrong.Take it; the turn is clean: A clean turn in a downtrend is a listed mistake.
wrong.Take it; downtrends bounce: A bounce is not our setup. The Go Signal is a leader in an uptrend.
wrong.Take it on the second candle only: The candle does not fix the trend.

questions.story: A first-hour reclaim of the prior close in a stock under every moving average, in a downtrend.

questions.q: What is wrong with that?
choices: The blind open buy; wait for the turn
Nothing; early is better
It is fine at half size
The stop should be wider
questions.answer: The blind open buy; wait for the turn
questions.why: It is the blind open buy. Buying the open before the turn gets stopped at the low. Wait for the stock to get back above the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Do not buy the red. Wait for the green.

wrong.Nothing; early is better: Buying the open before the turn gets stopped at the low. The turn is the signal.
wrong.It is fine at half size: Half size does not fix a buy before the turn.
wrong.The stop should be wider: A wider stop does not fix the timing.

questions.story: At 9:35 the stock is red, 1% under the prior close. You buy now to get ahead of the turn.

questions.q: Bought at 26.43, stop 25.66. The stock trades to 28.74. How many R is that?
questions.why: 3R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. That is where the first third comes off. VIAV got there in 3 days.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R. Three R is the first trim.

questions.q: What is it?
choices: A pivot, not a Go Signal
A Go Signal, a little late
An Oops at the prior low
A Remount of the prior close
questions.answer: A pivot, not a Go Signal
questions.why: A 30-minute pivot. AXON closed back above the prior close on the third candle, after the two-candle window. It is bought over the pivot candle's high.
questions.lesson_line: A third-candle turn is a pivot.

wrong.A Go Signal, a little late: There is no late version. After the second candle it is a pivot.
wrong.An Oops at the prior low: An Oops is a daily bar at the prior low.
wrong.A Remount of the prior close: A Remount follows a line lost over a long stay.

questions.story: The close back above the prior close, 359.35, comes on the third hourly candle at 361.39. Everything else passes.

questions.q: Is this a Go Signal?
choices: No; a bare turn with no flag
Yes, it turned inside the window
Yes, after earnings are best
Yes, if volume is heavy enough
questions.answer: No; a bare turn with no flag
questions.why: No. A red to green inside a wild post-earnings range, with no tight flag to buy against, is a bare red to green. SNOW did it and failed.
questions.lesson_line: No flag, no Go Signal. Just a common turn.

wrong.Yes, it turned inside the window: The clock is only one gate. The turn also needs the setup around it.
wrong.Yes, after earnings are best: A wild range after earnings leaves no tight flag to defend.
wrong.Yes, if volume is heavy enough: Volume is not the issue and it is not a rule.

questions.story: The stock swings wildly after earnings, with no tight flag. The first candle dips under the prior close and the next closes above it.

questions.q: Is this a Go Signal?
choices: No; a red to green in mid-air
Yes, it turned in the window
Yes, any dip under the close counts
Yes, if the market is Green
questions.answer: No; a red to green in mid-air
questions.why: No. A red to green in mid-air tested no level, so there is nothing to defend. CF was stopped the same session.
questions.lesson_line: No level tested, nothing to defend.

wrong.Yes, it turned in the window: On time, but the turn has to come at a level it can defend.
wrong.Yes, any dip under the close counts: The dip has to test the 20-day line or a marked level.
wrong.Yes, if the market is Green: A Green market does not supply a level.

questions.story: The first candle dips under the prior close and the next closes above it. The session low sits well above every moving average and marked level.

questions.q: Is this a Go Signal?
choices: Yes; candle two is in time
No; it needed the first candle
No; it is a pivot, not a signal
Only if volume is heavy too
questions.answer: Yes; candle two is in time
questions.why: Yes. The reclaim comes by the end of the second hourly candle. VIAV was the second-candle version and ran to 44.2R.
questions.lesson_line: First or second candle both count.

wrong.No; it needed the first candle: The first or the second candle counts. VIAV reclaimed on the second.
wrong.No; it is a pivot, not a signal: A pivot is a turn after the second candle. This one was on it.

questions.story: Candle one is red and stays under the prior close. Candle two closes green back above it.

questions.q: Go Signal or Oops?
choices: An Oops; a daily bar, prior low
A Go Signal; it reclaimed a line
A U&R of an older swing low
A Remount of the prior low
questions.answer: An Oops; a daily bar, prior low
questions.why: An Oops. An Oops gaps below the prior day's low and closes back above it on the daily bar. Deepvue and Williams define it at the prior low too.
questions.lesson_line: Daily bar and prior low: an Oops.

wrong.A Go Signal; it reclaimed a line: The Go Signal line is the prior close, read on the first two hourly candles.
wrong.A U&R of an older swing low: A U&R takes back a level over up to 3 sessions on the daily chart. This is one day at yesterday's low.
wrong.A Remount of the prior low: A Remount follows a line lost for days.

questions.story: On the daily chart, a stock gaps under yesterday's low and closes back above yesterday's low by the end of the day.

questions.q: Does it pass the context check?
choices: No; the 20-day is falling
Yes, it is above the 50-day
Yes, the turn is on time
Yes, but at half size only
questions.why: No. The card wants the 20-day EMA higher than it was 5 sessions ago. A falling 20-day fails the check.
questions.lesson_line: Context first: the 20-day EMA should be rising.

wrong.Yes, it is above the 50-day: Above the 50-day is one gate. The 20-day EMA has to be rising too.
wrong.Yes, the turn is on time: The clock is only one gate.
wrong.Yes, but at half size only: Half size does not fix a failed gate.

questions.story: A first-hour reclaim in a stock above its 50-day and 200-day. Its 20-day EMA is lower than it was 5 sessions ago.

questions.q: Can you tell?
choices: No; you need the hourly bars
Yes, the wick shows the dip
Yes, green means red to green
Yes, if volume is high
questions.answer: No; you need the hourly bars
questions.why: No. The daily footprint cannot show the turn, so grading from the daily chart is a listed mistake. Open the hourly bars.
questions.lesson_line: Daily wicks hide the clock. Use hourly bars.

wrong.Yes, the wick shows the dip: A wick could be made any time of day. The Go Signal lives in the first two hourly candles.
wrong.Yes, green means red to green: A green daily close says nothing about the first two hours.

questions.story: You look at a daily chart. A candle has a long lower wick and a green close. A friend calls it a Go Signal.

questions.q: Go Signal or pivot?
choices: A pivot over the candle high
A Go Signal, and a strong one
An Oops at the prior low
A U&R of a swing low
questions.answer: A pivot over the candle high
questions.why: A pivot. A turn later in the day, however clean, is a 30-minute pivot bought over the pivot candle's high.
questions.lesson_line: Clean but late is a pivot.

wrong.A Go Signal, and a strong one: Too late in the day for a Go Signal, however clean the candle.
wrong.An Oops at the prior low: An Oops is a daily bar at the prior low.
wrong.A U&R of a swing low: A U&R is a daily setup on a swing low.

questions.story: The stock reclaims the prior close at 13:30 on a clean green candle at the 20-day line.

questions.q: What does this trade teach?
choices: A big first candle widens the risk
A big first candle is a better signal
Never trade after 10:00
Always sell at the close
questions.answer: A big first candle widens the risk
questions.why: A big first candle widens the risk. NVDA's reclaim was the high of the day, the session closed under the prior close, and the stop was hit.
questions.lesson_line: A giant first candle leaves nothing to buy against.

wrong.A big first candle is a better signal: This one was the high of the day, and it was stopped the same session.
wrong.Never trade after 10:00: The window is the first two candles. The lesson is about the size of the first candle.
wrong.Always sell at the close: Selling at that close did not improve the average. The stop is the exit.

questions.story: The first candle closes at 126.81, up 2.3% and 2.7% from the stop. It was the high of the day. The session closes under the prior close.

questions.q: How do you file this?
choices: A planned loss; the stop was the exit
A mistake; you should have held
A reason to widen stops
A sign to drop the setup
questions.answer: A planned loss; the stop was the exit
questions.why: A planned loss. After the entry, a trade below the session low is the exit. The turn was real and TSLA gave it back within hours.
questions.lesson_line: The turn was real. The stock gave it back. The stop paid.

wrong.A mistake; you should have held: The stop is the exit. Holding through it is how a small loss gets big.
wrong.A reason to widen stops: The stop only moves up, never wider.
wrong.A sign to drop the setup: One stop says nothing about the setup. The edge shows over many trades.

questions.story: You bought at 361.86 after a green first candle. The third candle broke back under the prior close, and the fourth fell through your stop at 353.79.

questions.q: What is the read?
choices: A reclaim by a cent proves little
A perfect Go Signal
A pivot
An Oops
questions.answer: A reclaim by a cent proves little
questions.why: It proves little. CRWD reclaimed by one cent, the next candle fell straight through the stop, and the stock lost 6% in two sessions.
questions.lesson_line: A reclaim by a cent is not strength.

wrong.A perfect Go Signal: It meets the clock, but a one-cent reclaim has no strength behind it.
wrong.A pivot: It is in the first candle, so the window is met.
wrong.An Oops: An Oops is a daily bar at the prior low.

questions.story: A gap-down open reclaims the prior close, 64.03, by one cent at the close of the first candle. You are asked to buy at 64.04.

questions.q: Which grades higher?
choices: A; the strong first-candle turn
B; it waited for confirmation
Both grade the same, both in time
Neither; both are pivots
questions.why: A. A strong green hourly candle back above the prior close in the first candle is an A plus cue. A weak turn only in the second is a B minus cue.
questions.lesson_line: Strong and early grades higher than weak and late.

wrong.B; it waited for confirmation: A turn only in the second candle, and weak, is a B minus cue.
wrong.Both grade the same, both in time: The cues differ: a strong first candle is A plus, a weak second candle is B minus.
wrong.Neither; both are pivots: Both are inside the two-candle window, so both are Go Signals.

questions.story: Two Go Signals, both in time. A: a strong green first-candle reclaim. B: a weak turn only in the second candle.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell a big part into the climax
Hold it all, it is working
Add, momentum is strong
Move the stop below the 50-day
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the climax
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. On a climax run in your own long, sell a big part into the run; how big is a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: Sell into the vertical run.

wrong.Hold it all, it is working: On a climax run in your own long, sell a big part into it.
wrong.Add, momentum is strong: We do not add, and a climax is when to sell, not buy.

questions.story: Three days after the buy the stock is up sharply on its biggest range and gap of the run, a vertical climax.

questions.q: How do you read it?
choices: Thesis over; the stop is still the exit
Nothing; ignore the 50-day
Add on the dip
Move the stop to the 50-day
questions.answer: Thesis over; the stop is still the exit
questions.why: The pullback thesis is over, but the stop is still the exit. A close under the 20-day EMA is a warning; a close under the 50-day ends the thesis.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the 50-day ends the thesis. The stop still decides.

wrong.Nothing; ignore the 50-day: A close under the 50-day ends the pullback thesis.
wrong.Add on the dip: We do not add, least of all when the thesis is ending.
wrong.Move the stop to the 50-day: The stop only moves up, and the card keeps the session low as the stop.

questions.story: You hold a Go Signal. The stock closes under its 50-day, though your stop is not hit yet.

questions.q: The turn itself is the edge, because it happens in most sessions.
questions.why: False. The turn happens in about a third of all liquid sessions, so it is common. The stock and the level are the edge.
questions.lesson_line: The turn is common. The stock and the level are the edge.

questions.q: Which one is the Go Signal?
choices: A; in time, trend intact, Green
B; the candle is cleaner and bigger
C; the gap shows the most strength
None of the three
questions.answer: A; in time, trend intact, Green
questions.why: A. It dips under the prior close and reclaims by the second candle, with the trend intact and a Green market. B is a pivot and C never dipped.
questions.lesson_line: Dip, reclaim in time, trend and market in line.

wrong.B; the candle is cleaner and bigger: A turn at 13:30 is a pivot, however clean.
wrong.C; the gap shows the most strength: A gap up that never trades under the prior close is not a Go Signal.

questions.story: Three charts. A: a leader above its 50-day and 200-day, 20-day EMA rising, dips under the prior close and closes back above it in the second candle, Green market. B: the same, but the turn comes at 13:30. C: a gap up all morning.

questions.q: What is the new stop, and what do you do?
choices: The 23.85 low is the stop; hold
Out at once; a gap is a full loss
Move the stop back up to 24.48
Buy more at the 23.85 gap low
questions.answer: The 23.85 low is the stop; hold
questions.why: The 23.85 low is the new stop. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. Here that low is under 2R, so you hold to it.
questions.lesson_line: Gap through the stop: first 30-minute low, unless past 2R.

wrong.Out at once; a gap is a full loss: The rule hands the stop to the first 30-minute low, and out only if that is past 2R.
wrong.Move the stop back up to 24.48: 24.48 is above the gap, so it would sell at once. The gap rule uses the first 30-minute low.

questions.story: You bought a first-candle reclaim at 24.48 with the stop at 24.01. The next morning gaps through the stop. The first 30-minute low is 23.85.

questions.q: The stock's average daily volume is 400,000 shares. What is the most you may own at 1% of it?
questions.why: 4,000 shares. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume, so that you can always get out.
questions.lesson_line: One percent of daily volume is the ceiling.

questions.q: Which one is a pivot, not a Go Signal?
choices: A; the turn came after the second candle
B; the gap up
C; the falling 20-day EMA
All three
questions.answer: A; the turn came after the second candle
questions.why: A. A turn after the second hourly candle is a pivot, not a Go Signal. B has no dip under the prior close, and C fails the rising 20-day check.
questions.lesson_line: Late turn, pivot. No dip, no signal. Falling 20-day, pass.

wrong.B; the gap up: B never traded under the prior close, so there is no turn at all, not a pivot.
wrong.C; the falling 20-day EMA: C was in time, but the context check fails. That is a pass, not a pivot.
wrong.All three: Only A is a pivot. B has no dip and C fails the 20-day check.

questions.story: Three charts. A: the close back above the prior close comes on the third hourly candle. B: a gap up that never dips under the prior close. C: a reclaim in the first candle with the 20-day EMA falling.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a reason to pass a Go Signal?
choices: A rising 20-day EMA
A report in two sessions
A gap up that never dipped
A close under the 200-day
questions.why: A rising 20-day EMA. That is a point in its favour; the card wants it higher than it was 5 sessions ago. The other three are passes.
questions.lesson_line: A rising 20-day helps. The other three block the trade.

wrong.A report in two sessions: No new buy in the 3 sessions before an earnings report.
wrong.A gap up that never dipped: A gap up that never trades under the prior close is not a Go Signal.
wrong.A close under the 200-day: No longs below the 200-day simple moving average.

questions.q: Skip the buy if the stock is more than 10% above its 200-day average.
questions.why: False. The stretch test is against the 10-day average. Skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day.
questions.lesson_line: Ten percent over the 10-day: skip.

questions.q: A Go Signal is built in two half-size buys to average the price.
questions.why: False. Full size at once, one price, one stop. We do not add, and the size comes from the stop.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, no adding.
